cards.back: Show the PLATE/BLOCK alongside the print. Include artist proofs and edition numbers. Annotate each stage of the process. Show EXPERIMENTATION — vary ink density, paper type, colour combinations.

Students often make mistakes with this topic. Wrong: The print will look the same as the block or plate. Correct: Relief and intaglio prints are MIRROR IMAGES of the plate — text and directional elements will be reversed. Plan for this by working in reverse or accepting the reversal as part of the process.

Produce a series of prints using at least two different printmaking techniques. Annotate each print explaining the process, how you achieved different effects, and what you learned from comparing techniques.
AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of Printmaking Techniques using appropriate art vocabulary. Identify techniques, materials and processes accurately.

Printmaking Techniques is a fundamental aspect of GCSE Art and Design that connects to all four AQA assessment objectives. Understanding this topic requires both practical skill and contextual knowledge — you must apply techniques effectively AND explain how your work relates to other artists and designers. For printmaking techniques, effective experimentation means testing multiple approaches systematically. Start by researching how professional artists approach printmaking techniques, replicate their techniques as studies, then adapt and combine approaches to develop your own method.
